title: AAE Enforce Conformance Vector
description: Schema for a single vector against the enforce kernel (draft-kroehl-agentic-trust-aae-02: grants with type_fields, the closed constraint language, the verdict vocabulary and ratification). This schema EXTENDS the vector set; it does not replace schema/vector-schema.json, which continues to govern the 15 AAE-native vectors in vectors/ unchanged, nor schema/interop-composition-vector-schema.json. The three families cannot share one schema: a native vector is a JWS evaluated by the Section 5 nine-step algorithm and answers ACCEPT/REJECT at a numbered step, while an enforce vector is a mandate plus a transaction, carries no JWS and no step number, and answers PERMIT/DENY/PENDING with a recomputable core digest. Merging them would mean dropping 'secured_aae' from required and widening the result enum, which would let a native vector claim PERMIT and validate.

kernel.description: Which kernel the vector exercises. 'enforce_check' takes a mandate and a transaction; 'ratify' takes a prior verdict record, a decision and an authority proof. They are separate machines with separate domain tags and separate version constants.

kernel_version.description: The value the kernel writes into the core as enforce_version or ratify_version. Pinned in the vector because the domain tags are part of the digest: a kernel on a different version computes different digests over the same input, and a vector that did not say which version it was built against would be unfalsifiable.

domain_tags.description: The domain tags the expected digests were computed under, as ASCII without the trailing NUL separator. Present so a verifier can tell a tag mismatch from a logic mismatch when a digest fails to reproduce.

mandate.description: enforce_check: the mandate under evaluation. Deliberately untyped beyond 'any JSON value' — a vector that supplies a non-object mandate is a legitimate fail-closed case.

transaction.description: enforce_check: the transaction under evaluation, likewise untyped.

prior_record.description: ratify: the verdict record being ratified, as {core, core_digest}.

decision.description: ratify: the decision the authority asserts.

authority_proof.description: ratify: {mandate, authority, signature}. The public key is read from the mandate, never from the proof.

prev_core_digest.description: The chain link. Null or absent starts a chain. For a ratification it must equal the core digest of the record being ratified.

verdict.description: enforce_check outcome. PERMIT only on a bound grant whose constraints all hold with disposition allow; PENDING only on an explicit hold; everything else DENY.

status.description: ratify outcome. REJECTED leaves the prior record's verdict standing.

core_digest.description: The digest a conforming implementation must reproduce byte for byte from the input alone. This is the conformance target, not the verdict on its own.

reason_contains.description: A substring the reason must contain. A substring rather than the full string on purpose: draft -02 leaves the granularity of the reason text to the implementation (SHOULD, not MUST), so pinning it whole would test wording rather than behaviour.

error.description: ratify only: the caller error raised instead of producing a record. Guard 2 (a PERMIT is not ratifiable) and Guard 3 (the chain link points elsewhere) take this path — there is nothing to record when the question itself does not line up.

trace.description: The predicate trace. A vector may state a subset: every entry listed must appear in the produced trace with the same result, in the order given. It need not enumerate the whole trace.
